wrapp.note: Social gifting, later card-linked rewards; '$5.5 million in Series A funding ... led by Atomico' (TechCrunch, Nov 2011; Zennstrom to the board; Creandum's seed came earlier); the firm's 2013 release 'Wrapp raises $15m Series B'; acquired by Meniga Jan 2019 (Finovate), as Creandum and Greylock record

wunderloop.note: Listed on the firm's 2008-2011 sites (rendered 'wunderLOOP'; its own page /OurPortfolio/wunderLOOP.xml is in the CDX but the Internet Archive refused this machine before it could be read); no press, Wikipedia or register record identifies the company -> undetermined in every outcome column, excluded from every metric

xobni.note: Email and contacts add-in (Xobni, 'inbox' backwards); 'In March 2007, Xobni raised US$4.26 million from Vinod Khosla, First Round Capital, and Atomico' (Wikipedia; its GigaOM source is gone, and the round is unnamed) -> undetermined; acquired by Yahoo Jul 2013 for more than $60M (TechCrunch, which names Atomico among the backers)

y42.note: Low-code data platform; 'raised a $31 million Series A funding round co-led by Atomico and Insight Partners' (TechCrunch, Oct 2021; the firm's own post); no later round; operating (live site, 2025)

zapp.note: Quick-commerce delivery (London, 2020); Atomico was an investor in the $100M raised by Aug 2021 ('from various investors like Lightspeed, Atomico, 468 Capital, and Burda', UK Tech News) and joined by the Jan 2022 $200M Series B; the Mar 2021 round is unnamed -> undetermined; heavy cuts 2024, still trading Oct 2025

zattikka.note: Social/casual games group (Zattikka Ltd 2007; Zattikka PLC on AIM 2012, per the firm's own 2012 page); the register dates the position: Zattikka Ltd's annual return to 2009-09-26 lists Atomico Management Limited with 5,333 C ORDINARY shares (transferred 2010-06-24) - no round word; administration Aug 2013 (Game Developer), the PLC dissolved 2019 -> defunct

zocdoc.note: Doctor-booking marketplace (New York); 'The funding round was led by Baillie Gifford and Atomico' - the $130M round of Aug 2015 at $1.8B (Healthcare Dive; WSJ; the firm's own post), unnamed in every source; Francisco Partners' $150M of Feb 2021 disclosed no price, so the 2015 mark stands, stale; stage waits on the site-label score | Stage: the firm's own CMS files it under Stage 'Growth' (investment year 2014): the site label, eligible and scored 25/26 against the book's cited entry rounds (medium, under the 30-row bar)
